title: Spatial cell controls gave no clear change in floral pigment trends in six herbarium samples from 1941 to 2017
abstract: We tested whether added geographic controls changed time trends in floral UV pigment. Six tests used 858 herbarium specimens from Australia, Eurasia and North America in 1941-1985 and 1986-2017. We compared taxon-month and linear location controls with models that added taxon-specific 5-degree location cells. Cells required records from two distinct years. The trend changes ranged from -1.35 to +0.26 percentage points per decade. All six paired taxon-cluster intervals included zero after a six-test correction. Spatial controls retained 56-90% of residual time variation. Finer cells reduced the selected sample to 656 records. Grid, climate-control and equal-taxon checks also gave intervals across zero. The results do not show that geographic selection is harmless. Broad cells, sparse repeated records, nonrandom collection and uncertain cluster inference limit the test. The package gives code, exact source hashes, aggregate results, numerical checks and a figure. External record tables remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Time slopes with linear location controls and added taxon-specific geographic cells. Intervals use taxon clusters and a six-test multiplier. The primary tests concern paired slope changes, reported in the text. Right: residual time variation retained by added cells.
